title.es: Leer el ambiente de la conversación

es: Reconocer aperturas, señales de interés, cambios de tema y cierres en conversaciones informales entre desconocidos.

teaching.en: 'How do you know the bride?' is a safe opener at a wedding.
teaching.es: «¿De qué conoces a la novia?» es una apertura segura en una boda.
teaching.explanationEs: Un opener pregunta por el contexto compartido: es ligero y fácil de contestar.
segments: 'How do you know the bride?' is
a safe opener at a wedding.
teaching.audioText: 'How do you know the bride?' is a safe opener at a wedding.

teaching.en: At a wedding you mingle for hours, so every new acquaintance is a chance to talk.
teaching.es: En una boda socializas durante horas, así que cada conocido nuevo es una oportunidad de hablar.
teaching.explanationEs: Acquaintance es alguien a quien conoces poco; no equivale a friend.
segments: At a wedding you mingle for hours, so
every new acquaintance is a chance to talk.
teaching.audioText: At a wedding you mingle for hours, so every new acquaintance is a chance to talk.

teaching.en: She sounded genuine when she asked, 'Oh, really? How did that happen?'
teaching.es: Sonaba sincera cuando preguntó: «¿Ah, sí? ¿Cómo pasó eso?».
teaching.explanationEs: El interés genuino se nota en el eco («Oh, really?») y en la pregunta de detalle.
segments: She sounded genuine when she asked,
'Oh, really? How did that happen?'
teaching.audioText: She sounded genuine when she asked, 'Oh, really? How did that happen?'

teaching.en: A short answer and a quick look at the phone are a cue that someone wants to leave.
teaching.es: Una respuesta corta y una mirada rápida al móvil son una señal de que alguien quiere irse.
teaching.explanationEs: Cue es una pista que te ayuda a leer la situación.
segments: A short answer and a quick look at the
phone are a cue that someone wants to leave.
teaching.audioText: A short answer and a quick look at the phone are a cue that someone wants to leave.

teaching.en: If the talk gets awkward, steer it back to something easy, like the food or the music.
teaching.es: Si la charla se vuelve incómoda, reconduce hacia algo fácil, como la comida o la música.
teaching.explanationEs: Steer it back = volver con suavidad a un tema cómodo.
segments: If the talk gets awkward, steer it back to
something easy, like the food or the music.
teaching.audioText: If the talk gets awkward, steer it back to something easy, like the food or the music.

teaching.en: A warm closing is brief: 'It was great chatting, I'll let you get back to your friends.'
teaching.es: Un cierre cálido es breve: «Fue genial charlar, te dejo volver con tus amigos».
teaching.explanationEs: El cierre agradece, da un motivo y no se alarga.
segments: A warm closing is brief: 'It was great chatting,
I'll let you get back to your friends.'
teaching.audioText: A warm closing is brief: 'It was great chatting, I'll let you get back to your friends.'

es: Presentarse en pocas frases con un dato memorable y una pregunta que abra conversación, y usar coletillas para buscar acuerdo.

teaching.en: A bland introduction gives only your name and job, so nobody remembers it.
teaching.es: Una presentación sosa da solo tu nombre y tu trabajo, así que nadie la recuerda.
teaching.explanationEs: Bland describe algo sin sabor: aquí, una presentación sin nada personal.

and job, so nobody remembers it.
teaching.audioText: A bland introduction gives only your name and job, so nobody remembers it.

teaching.en: Add a hook: 'I'm Sara, a nurse who is learning to surf at forty.'
teaching.es: Añade un gancho: «Soy Sara, enfermera, y estoy aprendiendo a hacer surf a los cuarenta».
teaching.explanationEs: El hook es un dato concreto y sorprendente que se queda en la memoria.
segments: Add a hook: 'I'm Sara, a nurse

teaching.en: One small quirk makes you memorable: 'I bake bread at five every morning.'
teaching.es: Una pequeña rareza te hace memorable: «Hago pan a las cinco de la mañana».
teaching.explanationEs: Quirk es un hábito peculiar y simpático; memorable = fácil de recordar.
segments: One small quirk makes you memorable: 'I
bake bread at five every morning.'
teaching.audioText: One small quirk makes you memorable: 'I bake bread at five every morning.'

teaching.en: Keep the pitch short and end with a question: 'I design gardens. What about you?'
teaching.es: Mantén la presentación breve y termina con una pregunta: «Diseño jardines. ¿Y tú?».
teaching.explanationEs: Un pitch cabe en diez segundos; la pregunta final devuelve la palabra.
segments: Keep the pitch short and end with a

teaching.audioText: Keep the pitch short and end with a question: 'I design gardens. What about you?'

teaching.es: Una coletilla como «isn't it?» invita al otro a estar de acuerdo: «Es un lugar precioso, ¿verdad?».
teaching.explanationEs: Frase afirmativa + coletilla negativa; venue es el lugar donde se celebra el evento.
segments: A tag like 'isn't it?' invites the other person

es: Distinguir en un audio si una persona muestra interés genuino o solo cortesía a partir de ecos, reacciones breves y tono.

teaching.en: An echo question repeats part of what you heard: 'You moved to Quito?'
teaching.es: Una pregunta eco repite parte de lo que oíste: «¿Te mudaste a Quito?».
teaching.explanationEs: El eco sube al final y pide que el otro amplíe: es una señal de interés.
segments: An echo question repeats part of what
you heard: 'You moved to Quito?'
teaching.audioText: An echo question repeats part of what you heard: 'You moved to Quito?'

teaching.en: An enthusiastic voice rises and falls, but a flat voice stays on one note.
teaching.es: Una voz entusiasta sube y baja, pero una voz plana se queda en una sola nota.
teaching.explanationEs: El tono cuenta tanto como las palabras.
segments: An enthusiastic voice rises and falls, but
a flat voice stays on one note.
teaching.audioText: An enthusiastic voice rises and falls, but a flat voice stays on one note.

teaching.en: When a person hesitates before answering, the interest may be only courtesy.
teaching.es: Cuando una persona duda antes de responder, el interés puede ser solo cortesía.
teaching.explanationEs: Courtesy = cortesía: hacer lo correcto sin interés real.
segments: When a person hesitates before answering,
the interest may be only courtesy.
teaching.audioText: When a person hesitates before answering, the interest may be only courtesy.

teaching.en: 'That's interesting' can be a lukewarm reply, especially with no question after it.
teaching.es: «Qué interesante» puede ser una respuesta tibia, sobre todo si no va seguida de una pregunta.
teaching.explanationEs: En inglés británico, «interesting» a solas suele ser muy frío.
segments: 'That's interesting' can be a lukewarm reply,
especially with no question after it.
teaching.audioText: 'That's interesting' can be a lukewarm reply, especially with no question after it.

teaching.en: An eager listener will nod, lean forward and ask for more.
teaching.es: Un oyente interesado asentirá, se inclinará hacia delante y pedirá más.
teaching.explanationEs: Eager indica ganas de saber más; nod es asentir con la cabeza.
segments: An eager listener will nod, lean
forward and ask for more.
teaching.audioText: An eager listener will nod, lean forward and ask for more.

teaching.en: A bored listener looks at the clock, sighs and gives one-word answers.
teaching.es: Un oyente aburrido mira el reloj, suspira y da respuestas de una palabra.
teaching.explanationEs: Bored describe cómo se siente el oyente; boring, lo que le resulta aburrido.
segments: A bored listener looks at the

teaching.audioText: A bored listener looks at the clock, sighs and gives one-word answers.

es: Sostener una charla de ocho turnos con preguntas de seguimiento, ecos y una aportación personal equilibrada.

teaching.en: A follow-up question invites the other person to elaborate on one detail.
teaching.es: Una pregunta de seguimiento invita al otro a ampliar un detalle.
teaching.explanationEs: Elaborate = dar más detalles; la pregunta recoge algo que ya dijo.
segments: A follow-up question invites the other
person to elaborate on one detail.
teaching.audioText: A follow-up question invites the other person to elaborate on one detail.

teaching.en: Do not pry: 'How much do you earn?' is too personal for a first chat.
teaching.es: No fisgonees: «¿Cuánto ganas?» es demasiado personal para una primera charla.
teaching.explanationEs: Pry es preguntar cosas demasiado privadas; evita dinero, edad y política.
segments: Do not pry: 'How much do you earn?'
is too personal for a first chat.
teaching.audioText: Do not pry: 'How much do you earn?' is too personal for a first chat.

teaching.en: When she shares something, reciprocate with something of a similar size about yourself.
teaching.es: Cuando ella comparte algo, corresponde con algo de tamaño parecido sobre ti.
teaching.explanationEs: Reciprocate mantiene el equilibrio: ni solo escuchas ni solo hablas.
segments: When she shares something, reciprocate with something

teaching.audioText: When she shares something, reciprocate with something of a similar size about yourself.

teaching.en: If you ramble for a minute, the other person can only nod and wait.

segments: If you ramble for a minute, the
other person can only nod and wait.
teaching.audioText: If you ramble for a minute, the other person can only nod and wait.

segments: A short tangent is fine, but return to the

What was it like growing up in Manta? Mia: Loud and salty. I play the guitar on the beach. Do you run near Quito? Leo: Every morning, up in the hills. How did you start the guitar? Mia: My grandfather taught me, badly! Shall we find the cake? Leo: Great idea.
accepted: Mia: So, how do you know the bride? Leo: We studied together. And you? Mia: I'm her cousin. You studied engineering? Leo: Yes, and I run marathons to relax. What was it like growing up in Manta? Mia: Loud and salty. I play the guitar on the beach. Do you run near Quito? Leo: Every morning, up in the hills. How did you start the guitar? Mia: My grandfather taught me, badly! Shall we find the cake? Leo: Great idea.

Mia: How do you know the bride? Leo: We worked together. You? Mia: She's my cousin. You work in engineering? Leo: I'm an engineer, and I run marathons on weekends. You grew up in Manta, didn't you? What was that like? Mia: Beautiful. I play the guitar by the sea. Do you run in Quito? Leo: Yes, in the hills. How did you learn the guitar? Mia: My grandfather taught me! Shall we go and eat some cake? Leo: Sure, let's go.

feedback.es: La conversación alterna eco, aportación breve y preguntas de seguimiento sobre detalles que cada uno mencionó.

origin.text: Datos: Mia (enfermera, creció en Manta, toca la guitarra) y Leo (ingeniero, vive en Quito, corre maratones). Incluye un eco y una aportación personal breve de cada uno.

es: Abrir una conversación, crear afinidad, cerrarla y redactar un mensaje de seguimiento con recordatorio, detalle y propuesta concreta.

teaching.en: A vague message like 'Let's keep in touch' rarely leads to a second meeting.
teaching.es: Un mensaje vago como «Mantengámonos en contacto» rara vez lleva a un segundo encuentro.
teaching.explanationEs: Vague es lo contrario de concrete: sin día, hora ni plan.
segments: A vague message like 'Let's keep in
touch' rarely leads to a second meeting.
teaching.audioText: A vague message like 'Let's keep in touch' rarely leads to a second meeting.

teaching.en: Remind the person who you are and why you reach out: 'We met at the wedding, by the cake table.'
teaching.es: Recuerda a la persona quién eres y por qué le escribes: «Nos conocimos en la boda, junto a la mesa de los postres».
teaching.explanationEs: Reach out es contactar con alguien; remind + persona + dato.
segments: Remind the person who you are and why you reach
out: 'We met at the wedding, by the cake table.'
teaching.audioText: Remind the person who you are and why you reach out: 'We met at the wedding, by the cake table.'

teaching.en: A quick recap of one detail shows that you listened.
teaching.es: Un breve resumen de un detalle muestra que escuchaste.
teaching.explanationEs: Recap: menciona algo que dijo («You said you were training for a marathon»).
segments: A quick recap of one
detail shows that you listened.
teaching.audioText: A quick recap of one detail shows that you listened.

teaching.en: Then propose something concrete: 'Would you like to have coffee next Thursday at ten?'
teaching.es: Después propón algo concreto: «¿Te apetece tomar un café el próximo jueves a las diez?».
teaching.explanationEs: Concrete = día, hora y plan; en inglés se dice «have coffee», no «take a coffee».
segments: Then propose something concrete: 'Would you like
to have coffee next Thursday at ten?'
teaching.audioText: Then propose something concrete: 'Would you like to have coffee next Thursday at ten?'

teaching.en: End with a friendly sign-off, and remind the person that saying no is fine: 'No worries if you are busy.'
teaching.es: Termina con una despedida cordial y recuerda a la persona que puede decir que no: «No pasa nada si estás ocupado».
teaching.explanationEs: El sign-off cierra el mensaje; la salida fácil quita presión.
segments: End with a friendly sign-off, and remind the person that
saying no is fine: 'No worries if you are busy.'
